editorial:
Imagine a guy who knows everything about old treasures and how to sneak around the law. You get to follow a Romani antique dealer who doubles as a private eye, which makes for a really cool setup. The vibe is very classic 70s mystery, where the streets feel gritty and everyone has a secret. When one of his own friends is framed for a brutal murder, he has to use his street smarts and his knowledge of the art world to find the real killer. It feels like a cozy but tense detective story that keeps you guessing who is lying.

The acting is solid and the mystery actually holds up well. While the pacing is a bit slow at times, the twists make it worth the wait. If you like old-school crime stories, you will love the way the clues come together. Since it is an older TV movie, you might want to look for a remastered version.
endingExplained: The mystery wraps up when the detective finds a hidden piece of evidence that proves his friend was framed. He catches the real killer in a tense final confrontation where the murderer tries to cover their tracks by destroying the stolen art. In the end, the police arrive just in time to make the arrest. Your main hero clears his colleague's name and goes back to his antique shop, satisfied that justice was served.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old school detective stories and art mysteries.
